verdict.rationale: dlt provides a documented CLI (`dlt-docs-10`, `dlt-probe-5`) and Python API (`dlt.pipeline()/pipeline.run()`, `dlt-docs-29`) for scaffolding and running pipelines headlessly, plus a dedicated 'dltHub AI Harness' of skills, rules, and MCP servers explicitly built to let coding agents (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex) build, deploy, and run production pipelines (`dlt-docs-14`, `dlt-docs-58`, `dlt-docs-69`, `dlt-docs-80`, `dlt-probe-4`), including agent-driven scaffolding from OpenAPI specs (`dlt-docs-25`, `dlt-docs-32`) and one-command deploy (`dlt-docs-68`, `dlt-docs-11`). Missing for 10: independent/hands-on evidence of an agent actually performing the full scaffold-configure-run cycle end-to-end (all evidence is first-party docs), and a public OpenAPI spec for programmatic control was not found (`dlt-probe-3`).
